analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and a new `Traffic:` bullet in the `status` output documentation (head hunk around lines 998-1009). No executable code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, cache storage or authorization behavior is modified. The new text describes a status line stating whether the coordinator can route work to the connection: App Attest lease or legacy verification, plus causes such as disconnect, no verdict after 90 seconds, expired lease, locked keychain, stalled Apple call, App Attest unavailable, or no linked account. It references ServingReadiness.swift and StatusCommand+Traffic.swift, which were not supplied, so the described diagnostic behavior cannot be verified from this evidence. Relevant threat models are T-052, T-053 and T-057. The doc wording keeps authorization coordinator-owned and does not suggest local status grants serving permission. It does not widen trust or instruct disabling controls. The head excerpt supplied covers only lines 1-397, so the added bullet at roughly 998-1009 is visible only via the patch excerpt. The base text covers lines 1726-1974 and contains pre-existing documentation of environment passthrough and cache settings; these are unchanged. No concrete security regression is identified. Remaining question for integration: whether the `Traffic:` status output (implemented in unsupplied source) avoids leaking identifiers beyond what T-058 allows. It is only a doc description here and not evidenced as a problem.
